title: Smart Gate
brief: The SmartGate is an autonomous gate that uses real-time detection to protect endangered animal species. The technology behind it includes the Jetson Nano and TensorRT, which classify real-time images. The primary goal of this project is to redeploy the hardware and local software of the SmartGate to secondary development environment. Using the Current version available on GitHub, the gate will be built with the provided hardware and tested to ensure robust and repeatable operation.
scope: The team should also develop a chain of custody for any changes or work done on the SmartGate. The gate should be able to recognise different species of animals using the cameras and TensorRT model currently used by OpenSI as well as be manually operated through the prebuilt web interface. This project is a fantastic opportunity to make a real difference in wildlife conservation. By continuously developing the SmartGate system, we can better protect endangered species and ensure their safety.
requirements: 1. Embedded Systems: Familiarity with the Jetson Nano and other embedded systems. 2. Electrical Engineering: Knowledge of battery management and power supply systems. 3. Programming Skills: Proficiency in Python and C++ for hardware interfacing. 4. Machine Learning: Understanding of real-time image processing and TensorRT. 5. Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills to troubleshoot and resolve hardware and software issues. 6. Communication: Ability to document technical details and communicate effectively with the team. 7. Teamwork: Willingness to collaborate and work as part of a multidisciplinary team

title: Use of AI learnings
sponsor: Migrant and Refugee Settlement Services Australia (MARSS)
brief: The project involves the design and delivery of an information session for staff at the Migrant and Refugee Settlement Services (MARSS) on the use of AI technology in the workplace. The information program will need to be designed and delivered to staff over several sessions and include practical applications in the MARSS work environment. The students will also assess staff capability in AI usage before and after the delivery of the sessions and monitor their use in the workplace over a few weeks.
scope: The in-scope requirements of the project are 1. to design an information program for MARSS staff to be able to use AI in the workplace. 2. To deliver the program to MARSS staff 3. To evaluate the extent that staff have enhanced their abilities to use AI in the workplace as a result of the information sessions. Out of scope requirements include any actions other than the design, delivery and evaluation of AI training for staff to enable them to use in MARSS workplace.

title: An Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Mental Health Detection and Personalized Support Among Students
brief: This project proposes an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework for the early detection of mental health concerns and personalized support among students. The system employs machine learning models to analyze demographic, academic, lifestyle, and psychological assessment data to identify potential risks of stress, anxiety, and depression. Explainable AI techniques are integrated to provide transparent and interpretable predictions, enabling users to understand the factors influencing the results. Based on the identified risk level, the framework recommends personalized well-being strategies and support resources. The project emphasizes accuracy, transparency, privacy, and ethical AI to promote timely intervention and improve students' mental well-being.
scope: 1. Collect and preprocess publicly available student mental health datasets. 2. Develop machine learning models to detect mental health risks, including stress, anxiety, and depression. 3. Apply Explainable AI (XAI) techniques (e.g., SHAP or LIME) to provide interpretable predictions. 4. Design a user-friendly interface for mental health screening and result visualization. 5. Generate personalized well-being recommendations based on the predicted risk level. 6. Evaluate model performance using standard metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. 7. Ensure data privacy, ethical AI practices, and secure handling of user information. 8. Validate the proposed framework using benchmark datasets and comparative performance analysis.
requirements: 1. Python programming and software development skills. 2. Machine learning 3. Understanding of Explainable AI techniques (SHAP/LIME). 4. Basic web application development skills (Flask/Streamlit). 5. Database management knowledge. 6. Research, documentation, and technical communication skills.

title: AI-Based Vehicle Dent Detection and Damage Assessment System
brief: This project aims to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based system that automatically detects dents on vehicle surfaces using computer vision and deep learning techniques. The system analyzes images captured from a camera or mobile device and identifies dents by locating damaged regions on the vehicle body. An object detection model such as YOLO can be trained to recognize dents of different sizes and locations. The detected dents are highlighted with bounding boxes, enabling quick and accurate vehicle inspection. Out of scope: • Automatic repair cost estimation. • Vehicle owner identification or license plate recognition. • Detection of scratches, broken glass, rust, or paint peeling. • Real-time integration with insurance claim systems.
scope: • Collect and annotate vehicle images containing dents. • Develop a deep learning model to detect vehicle dents. • Identify the location and approximate size of dents. • Display detected dents with bounding boxes and confidence scores. • Evaluate the model using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. • Test the system on images captured under different lighting conditions
requirements: Python Programming Computer Vision (OpenCV) Deep Learning (TensorFlow or PyTorch) Object Detection (YOLO) Image Processing

title: Postpartum Depression Risk Prediction System with Explainable AI and Clinician Decision Support Dashboard
brief: Postpartum Depression (PPD) is a common mental health condition that affects mothers after childbirth. According to the World Health Organization, approximately 10–20% of new mothers experience postpartum depression, although many cases remain undiagnosed due to limited screening and social stigma. This project aims to develop an AI-powered clinical decision support system that predicts a mother's risk of developing postpartum depression using demographic, clinical, psychological, and lifestyle information. The system incorporates Explainable AI (XAI) techniques so that healthcare professionals understand why the model made a particular prediction, enabling trustworthy and transparent decision-making.
scope: 1. Develop an AI-Based Risk Prediction Model Design, train, and evaluate machine learning models to predict the risk of postpartum depression using demographic, clinical, psychological, and lifestyle data. 2. Implement Explainable AI (XAI) Integrate Explainable AI techniques (e.g., SHAP or LIME) to provide transparent, interpretable explanations for each prediction, enabling clinicians to understand the key contributing risk factors. 3. Develop a Web-Based Clinician Dashboard Build a secure dashboard that allows clinicians to enter patient information, view risk predictions, monitor patient history, and access visual explanations and summary reports. 4. Data Management and Visualization Develop modules for patient data collection, preprocessing, secure storage, and visualization of risk scores, trends, and feature importance through interactive charts and reports. 5. System Testing, Validation, and Deployment Validate the predictive model using standard performance metrics, conduct system testing, prepare technical documentation, and deploy a functional prototype for demonstration in a clinical decision-support setting.
requirements: 1. Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence Experience in developing, training, and evaluating machine learning models, including knowledge of classification algorithms and Explainable AI (SHAP/LIME). 2. Python Programming Proficiency in Python and libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, XGBoost/CatBoost, and Flask/FastAPI for AI model development and backend implementation. 3. Web Application Development Skills in front-end (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React/Angular) and back-end development to build a secure and user-friendly clinician dashboard. 4. Database Management Ability to design and manage relational databases (MySQL/PostgreSQL) for secure storage, retrieval, and management of patient data. 5. Software Engineering and Agile Development Knowledge of software design, API integration, testing, version control (Git/GitHub), and Agile methodologies for collaborative project development and delivery.

title: Team Plus Motorsport Wheel Alignment Sensor Development - Phase 2
brief: Team Plus designs and develops sensors, displays and applications for motorsport data collection and analysis. We have begun development of a new sensor to our portfolio that measures wheel alignment data and may help teams reduce the time needed to measure and adjust these critical setting at a race track as well as helping any DIY car enthusiast do home measurements of alignment. This project will build upon the experience of student groups last semester and continue to develop the software running on the sensor using Arduino C++ on prototype ESP32 based sensors. Some interest in motor vehicles and/or motorsport may help but is not required. This is a software development project. NOTE: If possible, the Sponsor (Team Plus) will organise a closed road session during the semester at a driver training centre towards the end of the semester to provide a real life test of the prototype hardware and software using the Team Plus race car.
scope: The new Team Plus Wheel Alignment sensor is an IOT device consisting of an ESP32 microprocessor based solution combined with a 9 way motion sensor and small battery that is intended to be mounted in each wheel hub of a race car plus a 5th sensor mounted to a fixed location in the car as a reference point. The aim of this project is to learn from previous semester efforts and complete a fully working firmware/software for the sensors and display app. In this “phase 2” of the Research and Development of this potential project, the plan is to develop a working proof of concept sensor software for all 4 wheels plus the fixed point sensor that can measure and transmit live over Bluetooth to a web or phone app acting as a hand held console screen to view and record the data the current wheel alignment data for that wheel including: - Camber angle - Toe angle note: these terms will be explained by sponsor. Some prototype sensor hardware will be provided and previous team software code. You may choose to request additional or different processor and sensor boards if you wish and redesign the sensor enclosures if needed (and if there is time) Scope of Work: Minimum requirement: - Research calculations required to calculate the required alignment settings. Expect you to use AI or similar to assist with this, and some previous code by previous teams will be provided - Develop working firmware in Arduino IDE for the provided prototype wheel sensor that can: - Develop a calibration process to get sensors prepared for measurement - Measure current angles of wheel Camber and Toe using fixed body sensor as reference point. - Transmit current angles of wheel Camper and Toe over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) which can be monitored by bluetooth phone app to see the results. - Minimum requirement is that this calculates and transmits data live when car is stationary. - Develop working firmware in Arduino IDE for the provided prototype fixed point sensor that can: - Calibrate the fixed point sensor to learn its relative position to car direction of travel and ground level. - provide position and angle data of fixed point sensor over bluetooth for wheel sensor to use for calculations. - Test Plan including demonstrating results match a manual method of measuring the alignment. - Documentation within the code and in technical documentation to explain to next team how it all works. Desirable: - Add Caster calculations to wheel sensor - Data calculates and transmits angles live when vehicle is in motion. • Deliver the resulting app code and implementation documentation to sponsor in a github.com repository.
requirements: Desired Skills: • App development skills • Real time code development in C++ / Arduino or willingness to learn it. • Project Management • Some interest in cars and motorsport may be an advantage but not necessary Note: • Some car driving sessions for testing solutions may be organised by sponsor at a closed road facility during the semester that will require each student to sign an activity injury liability waiver. • This project uses and develops the sponsors (Team Plus) Intellectual Property and may require signing a deed of agreement to maintain the sponsors protections. This is organised using standard University provided templates.

title: AI Race Track Driving Coach App
brief: Team Plus designs, manufactures and sells a range of innovative sensors, phone apps and display devices for motorsport capturing live IOT data helping the safety and performance of race drivers. This includes sensors devices that capture live tyre temperatures, pressures and brake temperatures at with 10 updates per second. This project aims to develop an app which can import data recorded from a race track session and use AI to provide advice to the driver on how to improve their lap times. This could include advice on driving lines, braking, steering and acceleration techniques as well as basic car setup changes such as tyre pressures and camber settings. Note: If possible, the Sponsor (Team Plus) will organise a closed road session during the semester at a driver training centre towards the end of the semester to provide a real life test of the prototype app software using the Team Plus race car.
scope: Team Plus motorsport devices and other motorsport focused data logging devices can capture a large range of parameters during a session on a track. That can include GPS position, speed, directions, G-forces and car data like accelerator position, RPM, Steering angles, tyre pressures and tyre temperature patterns. This data is often analysed by driver, engineers or others to provide insights into how the car is performing and opportunities to improve the lap times. There are emerging attempts in the market to utilise AI to automate some of this advice and data analysis. Scope of Work: • Learn the existing functionality and data collected from Team Plus sensors and motorsport logging tools. • Develop a prototype web app that can import the data for a session and provide valuable driver advice to improve lap times. • At a minimum the AI should provide advice on tyre pressure and camber improvements based on the tyre temperature and pressure data. • It would be desirable to analyse driver braking performance, racing line around the track and any other driver tips to improve laptime. • Team should deliver the resulting app code and implementation documentation to sponsor in a github.com repository and provide a formal handover of the results of the project.
requirements: • App development skills • AI skills • Project Management • User interface design – frontend • Some interest in cars and motorsport may be an advantage but not necessary

title: Enhancing Hospital Flow to Improve Patient Care and Readmission Outcomes
brief: According to the Australian Medical Association’s 2025 Public Hospital Report Card, Australian hospitals face growing pressure from rising demand, workforce constraints, limited bed availability, and emergency department congestion. Large volumes of administrative and electronic health record (EHR) data are collected, yet translating this information into actionable insights remains challenging. SAS, a global leader in analytics, supports more than 1,700 health and social services organisations worldwide, helping improve patient outcomes and operational efficiency. This highlights the need for applied analytics approaches that enable students to explore how data can improve hospital workflows, patient outcomes, and overall system efficiency.
scope: The project involves working with a de-identified hospital dataset to investigate patient hospitalisation patterns, readmissions, length of stay, and resource utilisation using SAS analytics tools. Students will undertake data preparation, cleaning, and exploration, followed by exploratory and descriptive analysis of patient and hospital activity to identify patterns and factors associated with readmission risk and length of stay. Where appropriate, the project may include the development and evaluation of predictive or statistical models, patient cohort segmentation, and pathway analysis. Students will communicate findings through dashboards, visualisations, and written reports, develop evidence-based recommendations supported by analysis, and present outcomes to both academic and industry stakeholders. As a student capstone project, the emphasis is on applying analytical, teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills rather than delivering production-ready solutions. Success will be measured by the quality of the analysis, insights, recommendations, and professional project delivery.
requirements: This project assumes that students have a foundational level of technical and analytical skills. Students should be comfortable with data wrangling, including cleaning, transforming, and working with structured datasets such as hospital electronic health records, and possess basic programming skills, particularly in SAS (the primary tool), with familiarity in Python, R, or SQL being advantageous. The project also requires competency in data visualisation to present insights through dashboards and charts, as well as an understanding of statistical analysis and modelling, including descriptive and diagnostic techniques to explore trends and relationships. Additionally, some exposure to predictive modelling, such as regression or classification, is expected to analyse outcomes like readmission risk or length of stay, although more advanced machine learning techniques are not required. Overall, students should be able to apply an end-to-end analytics workflow from data preparation and exploration to modelling and visualisation while demonstrating critical thinking, problem-solving, and clear communication of insights.

title: Applied Sovereign AI: Rapid Prototyping Micro-SaaS Solutions with Agentaus
brief: The commercial technology sector is rapidly shifting from building foundational AI models to applying commercial APIs to solve niche, high-value problems. However, integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into targeted applications involves complex, infrequently-encountered issues: mitigating AI hallucinations, designing dynamic prompt architectures, and ensuring data privacy. This project operates as an "Applied AI Innovation Sprint." Using Trellis Data’s sovereign Agentaus API, student teams will be tasked with identifying a specific, real-world "micro-friction" (e.g., local business workflow inefficiencies, student productivity bottlenecks, or niche data processing tasks) and rapidly prototyping a functional AI-driven application to solve it. Because the specific use-case is student-defined, there is no obvious, standard-practice solution. Students must engage in conceptual thinking to define their own diverse stakeholder needs, design an analytical approach to evaluate AI output accuracy, and navigate the conflicting technical constraints of time budgets versus feature creep. This project provides hands-on, enterprise-level experience with commercial AI integration, bridging the gap between theoretical computing and rapid market deployment.
scope: Identify the high-level in-scope requirements and activities of the project. • Problem Scoping & System Analysis: Identifying a specific, narrow user friction point (e.g., student workflow, local retail data sorting) that can be solved using an LLM. • Prompt Engineering & Architecture: Designing, testing, and refining dynamic prompts to ensure the Agentaus API delivers accurate, contextually relevant, and hallucination-free outputs. • API Integration: Successfully connecting a lightweight front-end or script to the Agentaus API via standard REST/JSON protocols. • Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Development: Building a basic, functional user interface (Web app, CLI, or simple dashboard) to interact with the AI model. • Evaluation & Testing: Developing an analytical framework to test the AI's accuracy, latency, and usability against the original problem statement. • Agile Project Management: Delivering the prototype within a strict 10-week (approx. 10-day effort) timebox using agile sprints.
requirements: Identify the skillsets required of the project. • Software Development / Coding: Proficiency in Python or JavaScript/TypeScript. • API Integration: Experience or willingness to learn RESTful APIs and JSON data handling. • Applied Artificial Intelligence: Basic understanding of LLMs, prompt engineering, and context window management. • Web Development: Basic front-end skills (HTML, CSS, React/Vue, or Python frameworks like Streamlit/Flask) to build the user interface. • Business / System Analysis: Ability to define user requirements and translate a messy real-world problem into a logical software architecture. • Agile Project Management: Ability to prioritise features, manage a tight time budget, and execute weekly sprint deliverables.

title: CareSync: Offline-Capable Mobile Logging for Community Health Field Visits
brief: Community and home care workers regularly visit clients in their homes, aged care facilities, or remote/rural locations across the ACT and surrounding NSW regions — many of which have unreliable or no mobile connectivity. Currently, visit notes, care task checklists, and client observations are often recorded on paper or in disconnected apps that require an active internet connection, leading to delays, data loss, and duplicated administrative work. This project involves designing and developing a mobile application that enables community health and care workers to log client visits, complete structured care checklists, record observations and task completion, and capture supporting notes — all while fully offline. Data entered offline is securely queued on the device and automatically synchronised with a central system once connectivity is restored, with conflict handling for cases where multiple updates occur before syncing.
scope: 1.Mobile application (Android and/or iOS) for care workers to log client visits and complete care checklists 2.Offline data capture: forms, checklists, and notes can be filled in without an internet connection 3.Local on-device storage of unsynced data (e.g. SQLite or equivalent local-first database) 4.Automatic background synchronisation to a central server/database once connectivity is restored 5.Basic conflict handling for offline entries (e.g. timestamp-based resolution, flagging conflicts for review) 6.User authentication and role-based access (care worker vs supervisor/admin) 7.Digital checklist builder or pre-configured checklist templates (e.g. medication check, mobility support, wellbeing 8.observation)Photo attachment support for visit notes (optional, if relevant to sponsor's use case) 9.GPS/timestamp capture to verify visit location and completion time 10.Simple web-based dashboard for supervisors to view submitted visit logs and flag incomplete/overdue visits 11.Basic data security measures (encrypted local storage, secure transmission, login authentication) 12.Test/demo dataset using de-identified sample data (no real client information)
requirements: Core Technical: 1.Mobile app development fundamentals (Flutter/Dart or React Native/JavaScript-TypeScript) 2.Basic database concepts (SQL/NoSQL, local vs. remote storage) 3.REST API design and consumption (or willingness to learn Firebase/Supabase) 4.Version control (Git/GitHub) for team collaboration 5.Basic UI/UX design principles for mobile interfaces Helpful but Not Essential: 1.Experience with offline-first or local-first app architecture 2.Familiarity with cloud backend services (Firebase, Supabase, AWS Amplify, or similar) 3.Basic understanding of data privacy/security principles (especially relevant given health-related data) 4.Experience with state management in mobile apps (Provider/Riverpod for Flutter, Redux/Context API for React Native)

title: Installation and performance comparison of open-source 5G cores on the Cisco Unified Edge for AI-based intrusion detection

ICC recently acquired a cutting-edge computing device from Cisco that should be able to run complete versions of 5G cores. Open-source versions of the 5G core will enable us to investigate novel AI-based intrusion detection software for control traffic. Various 5G cores exist in open source, but it is unclear which of those would suit ICC most, if any. The aim of the project is to install these cores on the Cisco Unified Edge and compare their performance in terms of the ability to carry an AI workload.
scope: Hardware- and (Linux-based) software-integration and testing and validation of cutting-edge networking and computing equipment and software stacks. Although a basic understanding of coding is needed, this project will not require much (if any) actual coding. Advanced understanding of mobile networking and cyber security is a pre but not required, as various other ICC members can provide that input.

It also requires communication and teamworking skills to be able to collaborate with Cisco engineers and, possibly, academics from Singapore. title: AI–Blockchain Hybrid Intrusion Detection System
brief: Design and implement a hybrid Intrusion Detection System (IDS) that combines a machine learning/deep learning detection engine with a blockchain layer for tamper-proof logging and auditability. Every classification decision (normal/attack, attack type, confidence score) made by the AI model is hashed and recorded on a blockchain ledger, ensuring the detection history cannot be silently altered — even by an insider with database access. This directly extends existing hybrid ML/DL IDS work (e.g., ensemble or hybrid models like CNN-LSTM, HMKELM-MTLBO-IDBSCAN) by adding a trust and traceability layer.
scope: Training/evaluating ML/DL models (existing or new hybrid models) on IDS datasets (e.g., CICIDS2017, NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15) Designing a lightweight blockchain (private/permissioned, e.g., Hyperledger Fabric or a custom chain) for logging detection events Smart contract logic for immutable event logging and access control Comparative performance evaluation: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, latency overhead with vs. without blockchain logging Visualization dashboard comparing model performance across datasets
requirements: Python (scikit-learn, TensorFlow/PyTorch) for ML/DL model development Familiarity with IDS/network traffic datasets and preprocessing Blockchain basics: Hyperledger Fabric, Ethereum (Solidity), or Ganache/Truffle for prototyping Smart contract development (Solidity) if using Ethereum-based chain Data visualization (Chart.js, Matplotlib, or similar) Basic understanding of consensus mechanisms (PoW/PoA/PBFT)

title: AI-Powered Early Autism Screening and Developmental Support System
brief: The project aims to develop an AI-powered early autism screening and developmental support system that identifies potential behavioral and communication indicators associated with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The system analyzes multimodal data such as facial expressions, eye-gaze patterns, speech characteristics, and behavioral interactions using computer vision, natural language processing, and deep learning techniques. It provides early screening insights, developmental progress tracking, and personalized activity recommendations for children while maintaining privacy, fairness, and ethical AI practices. The proposed solution assists parents, educators, and healthcare professionals in enabling timely intervention and support, without replacing clinical diagnosis.
scope: Collect and preprocess relevant child behavioral, speech, video, and questionnaire-based datasets for autism screening research. Develop a multimodal AI pipeline combining video, audio, and behavioral data analysis. Implement computer vision techniques for analyzing facial expressions, eye-gaze patterns, attention, and interaction behaviors. Develop speech and audio analysis modules to identify communication patterns, speech delays, and vocal characteristics. Apply machine learning and deep learning models to identify behavioral indicators associated with autism spectrum characteristics. Develop a risk assessment model that categorizes developmental indicators into different levels (e.g., low concern, moderate concern, requires further assessment). Integrate standardized screening questionnaire data to enhance AI-based assessment. Develop a personalized recommendation module for suggesting developmental activities and learning support strategies. Create a user-friendly web/mobile dashboard for parents, caregivers, or educators to view assessment insights and progress tracking. Implement explainable AI techniques to improve transparency of predictions. Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Ensure ethical AI practices including child data privacy, secure data handling, bias mitigation, and responsible usage guidelines.
requirements: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) concepts for developing predictive models. Deep Learning techniques for behavioral, speech, and image-based analysis. Computer Vision skills for facial expression analysis, eye-gaze tracking, activity recognition, and video processing. Natural Language Processing (NLP) for speech analysis, communication pattern understanding, and text-based assessment. Python Programming with libraries such as NumPy, Pandas, OpenCV, Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, and PyTorch. Audio and Speech Processing techniques for extracting features from child vocal patterns. Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering for handling multimodal datasets (video, audio, and behavioral data). Machine Learning Model Development and Evaluation using algorithms such as CNN, LSTM, Transformers, Random Forest, and XGBoost. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques for improving model transparency and interpretation. Web/Mobile Application Development using frameworks such as Flask, FastAPI, Streamlit, React, Flutter, or similar technologies. Database Management (SQL/NoSQL) for secure storage and management of user and assessment data. Data Visualization and Analytics for presenting behavioral trends and developmental progress. Software Engineering Practices including Git/GitHub, testing, documentation, and version control.

title: Software Trading Post: A Whole-of-Government Licence Reallocation Platform
brief: Design and prototype a proof-of-concept Software Trading Post platform that helps government agencies reuse software licences that would otherwise go unused. Agencies can list surplus licences they no longer need and register demand for additional licences, allowing licences to be transferred between departments instead of purchasing new ones. The platform will match surplus licences with demand, and support licence transfer requests between departments, while maintaining a record of licence listings, requests, approvals and transfers. The solution will initially focus on Microsoft licences initially but should support expansion to other vendors.
scope: Stakeholder analysis and requirements gathering; solution design and architecture; and prototyping of a Software Trading Post platform. The MVP includes management of surplus software licence listings and licence demand requests, matching of licence supply and demand, and recording and tracking of listings, requests and transfers. Stretch goals may include bulk data import, notifications, authentication and access controls, advanced matching and allocation rules, cost-recovery or trade models, AI-assisted recommendations, and support for additional software vendors or asset types.
requirements: Business and systems analysis, stakeholder engagement, requirements elicitation, solution architecture and design, UX design, web application development, database design, testing, Agile project delivery, and technical documentation. AI-supported development and prototyping optional.

title: Advancing Alzheimer’s diagnosis through biomarkers using agentic AI
brief: To advance Alzheimer’s diagnosis, we need to combine diverse biomarkers with smart computational tools. Agentic AI systems autonomously analyze multimodal data including cerebrospinal fluid proteins, plasma proteomics, neuroimaging, and digital behavioral signals to detect early pathological changes and predict disease progression. These tools combine machine learning with explainable frameworks, improving clinical decision-making, reducing diagnostic delays and allowing for customized treatment strategies. In addition, ongoing surveillance and digital phenotyping thru wearables extend the range of biomarkers beyond traditional laboratory measures. The combination of agentic AI and biomarker science promises earlier, more accurate and ethically responsible detection of Alzheimer’s, transforming patient care and accelerating therapeutic development.
scope: The project requires defining biomarker selection, establishing data integration pipelines, and deploying agentic AI models. Activities include collecting multimodal datasets (CSF, plasma, imaging, digital signals), developing explainable AI frameworks, validating outputs with clinical partners, and ensuring ethical compliance. Continuous monitoring via wearables and iterative model refinement are also in scope. The project emphasizes early detection, personalized progression tracking, and integration into clinical workflows.
requirements: Students should be comfortable with machine learning and data science, since they’ll be designing predictive models and working with complex biomarker datasets. Bioinformatics skills are crucial for making sense of proteomic and genomic data. On the technical side, software development will be needed to build pipelines and create clinical dashboards. Finally, strong abilities in business/system analysis and business analytics will ensure the project stays aligned with healthcare needs and delivers meaningful outcomes.

title: Anomaly Detection
brief: For your capstone project, develop an anomaly detection approach to identify irregularities in real-world datasets, such as financial transactions (e.g., fraudulent activities) or healthcare data (e.g., abnormal patient vitals like heart rate or blood pressure). You will collect and preprocess cross-sectional or time series data from public sources. Implement machine learning models, such as Isolation Forest or LSTM, to detect anomalies, evaluating their performance using metrics like precision, recall, and F1-score. Visualise detected anomalies and patterns to provide actionable insights, enhancing your skills in data analysis, machine learning, and Python or R programming. Optionally, deploy the model as a web-based dashboard to showcase real-time anomaly detection capabilities. Out of Scope:• Developing proprietary data collection systems or hardware for real-time financial or healthcare data acquisition. • Implementing complex financial trading platforms or clinical decision support systems based on detected anomalies. • Using paid or proprietary datasets requiring subscriptions beyond freely available public sources. • Integrating with live external systems, such as real-time banking platforms or hospital EHR systems.

title: Time Series Analysis Using Regression and Machine Learning Models

This project examines classical regression-based time series models and modern machine learning approaches for analysing and predicting temporal data. Methods such as linear and nonlinear regression, ARIMA-type models, and selected machine learning models will be explored and compared. The project will apply these techniques to real-world financial time series, such as asset prices or returns, as well as other relevant datasets. title: Simulating Autonomous Robot Swarms
brief: Want to create the world a robot swarm lives in and the intelligence that drives it? Join our capstone project to build a Python-based simulation environment and program a swarm of autonomous robots that navigate, coordinate, and complete missions together, no human control needed. Your work will directly power a research study on how people supervise robotic swarms. This is your chance to level up your coding skills and work on something that could shape the future of robotics!
scope: You will develop two tightly connected pieces: the environment and the swarm that operates inside it: 1. The Simulation Environment A configurable 2D operational area with obstacles, waypoints, and task zones (e.g., search areas, delivery points, inspection targets). Scenario configuration via simple files (JSON) so researchers can change layouts, mission types, and difficulty without touching code. Environmental dynamics such as moving obstacles or changing task locations to keep the swarm challenged. 2. The Swarm Swarm behaviours that run on their own: flocking (separation, alignment, cohesion), formation keeping, and collision avoidance. Task allocation: the swarm autonomously divides up work such as area coverage, target search, and point-to-point delivery. Imperfect agents: individual robots can drift off course, drop out, or misreport status creating realistic events for a human supervisor to catch. You will add controls to scale the swarm size and adjust behaviour parameters (speed, spacing, autonomy level), build a dashboard to visualise the swarm in action, and stream task and swarm-state data (timestamped logs) to an external system for analysis (not part of the project). Your work will help researchers study how humans monitor and intervene in swarm operations during a pilot study.
requirements: Python programming

title: Intelligent Network Security: AI/ML-Based Predictive Maintenance for Network Devices
brief: This experimental capstone project will develop an AI/ML-based predictive maintenance system to improve the security and reliability of network devices. Using real equipment in a controlled laboratory, students will collect operational data such as temperature, voltage, current, power, processor and memory utilisation, interface errors, packet loss, latency, throughput, retransmissions, and availability. Safe scenarios will simulate normal operation, degradation, faults, and selected cyber anomalies. The resulting time-series data will support anomaly detection, health classification, fault prediction, and early warning. A dashboard will clearly present device health, alerts, and recommended maintenance actions.
scope: • Experimental implementation using real network devices. • Collection of device-health and network-performance data. • Development and comparison of selected AI/ML models. • Detection of abnormal device behaviour and potential faults. • Generation of predictive maintenance and security alerts. • Development of a basic monitoring dashboard. • Evaluation of model accuracy, false alarms, and early-warning capability.
requirements: • Basic knowledge of computer networks, network devices, and cybersecurity. • Programming skills, preferably in Python. • Introductory understanding of AI/ML and data analytics. • Familiarity with network configuration, monitoring, and troubleshooting tools. • Basic understanding of Linux, databases, and data visualisation. • Experimental, problem-solving, teamwork, documentation, and presentation skills.

title: RF Fingerprinting for Wireless Device Identification and Rogue Transmitter Detection using AI/ML
brief: This capstone project will develop an AI/ML-based RF fingerprinting system to identify wireless transmitters from unique hardware-induced signal characteristics. Using a software-defined radio in a controlled laboratory, students will capture I/Q signal samples from several low-power wireless devices. The project will cover signal preprocessing, feature extraction, dataset preparation, and transmitter classification. Students will evaluate how distance, channel conditions, transmission power, and repeated measurements affect performance. A lightweight prototype will identify authorised devices and flag unknown transmitters, with results assessed using classification and robustness metrics under changing operating conditions.
scope: • Review of RF fingerprinting and device-identification methods. • SDR-based collection of I/Q samples from several wireless devices. • Dataset labelling, preprocessing, and feature extraction. • Development and comparison of selected AI/ML models. • Identification of authorised devices and detection of unknown transmitters. • Evaluation under different distances and channel conditions. • Development of a basic prototype or dashboard.
requirements: • Basic knowledge of wireless communications and RF systems. • Familiarity with digital signal processing and I/Q data. • Programming skills, preferably in Python. • Introductory understanding of AI/ML and data analysis. • Basic experience with SDR tools and experimental testing. • Teamwork, problem-solving, documentation, and presentation skills.

title: ML-based Structural Health Monitoring and Anomaly Detection of a Physical Infrastructure (e.g., Building, bridge, etc.)
brief: This project focuses on developing a machine learning (ML) based structural health monitoring (SHM) system for a bridge. Students will simulate or collect sensor data (e.g., vibration, strain, tilt, temperature, acceleration, cracks) and design a data-driven framework to detect anomalies and predict structural degradation. The project will involve signal preprocessing, feature extraction (time/frequency domain), and ML model development for damage classification or remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. A prototype dashboard will be developed to visualise structural condition in near real-time. The outcome will demonstrate how AI-enabled monitoring can enhance infrastructure safety, predictive maintenance, and cost-effective asset management.

title: ThinkGrasp-Lite: Reproducing and Optimizing Vision-Language Grasping in Clutter with Open-Source VLMs
brief: The goal of this project is to reproduce the ThinkGrasp pipeline, a state-of-the-art robotic grasping system that uses Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to reason about and grasp objects in heavily cluttered environments. While the original paper relies on the commercial GPT-4o API, this student project will focus on reproducing the simulation environment and attempting to replace the costly closed-source model with open-source alternatives (e.g., LLaVA, Qwen-VL) to achieve a more accessible and autonomous system. The system will interpret natural language commands (e.g., "Pick up the red apple under the box") and execute multi-step manipulation (removing obstacles first).
scope: Pipeline Reproduction (Existing Resources): 1. Deploy the official ThinkGrasp code (Open Source). 2. Integrate the segmentation module (LangSAM / VLPart) and grasp generation module (GraspNet or similar) as described in the paper. 3. Set up the simulation environment (likely PyBullet or Isaac Gym) to replicate the "cluttered desk" scenarios. Model Substitution (New Challenge): 1. Replace the reasoning core (GPT-4o) with an open-source VLM (e.g., LLaVA-Next, Qwen-VL-Chat, or DeepSeek-VL) to evaluate if smaller, local models can handle the "strategic reasoning" required for removing obstacles. Performance Benchmarking: 1. Compare the success rate (Success Rate) and planning time between the GPT-4o version and the open-source VLM version.

title: Fine-Tuning Strategies for Physics-Aware Suction Grasping: A Data-Centric Simulation Study
brief: This project focuses on the fine-tuning and domain adaptation of deep neural networks for the specific task of robotic suction grasping. Unlike standard object detection, suction grasping requires predicting invisible physical properties: Seal (airtightness) and Wrench (resistance to gravity/torque). Students will utilize the SuctionNet-1Billion dataset to investigate how different fine-tuning strategies (e.g., Layer Freezing, Differential Learning Rates, or Loss re-weighting) affect a model's ability to learn these physical constraints. The goal is to determine the optimal training recipe that allows a standard vision backbone (e.g., ResNet-50 or ViT) to generalize to unseen, cluttered 3D objects in simulation.
scope: Backbone Pre-training Analysis: Compare the starting point efficacy: ImageNet pre-trained weights vs. PointNet (geometric) pre-trained weights. Fine-tuning Experimentation: Layer-wise Analysis: Systematically freeze different stages of the backbone to determine which layers capture the "surface geometry" required for suction. Loss Function Engineering: Design and fine-tune a composite loss function that balances classification (Suctionable or not) and regression (Seal/Wrench scores), addressing the data imbalance problem. Hyperparameter Sweeping: rigorous testing of learning rate schedulers (Cosine Annealing vs. Step Decay) to optimize convergence speed and final accuracy. Simulation-based Evaluation: Use the SuctionNet simulation API to run inference on the test set and generate heatmaps. Evaluation is purely metric-based: Mean Perfection Rate (MPR) and Success Rate at different error tolerances.
requirements: Deep Learning Theory: Deep understanding of Backpropagation, Overfitting, Regularization, and Transfer Learning mechanisms. PyTorch/TensorFlow: Ability to write custom training loops, custom Loss functions, and use hooks to visualize gradients. Experiment Tracking: Proficiency with tools like Weights & Biases (WandB) or TensorBoard to visualize loss curves and compare dozens of training runs. Data Analysis: Ability to analyze confusion matrices and regression error distributions to diagnose "why the model failed."

title: Interactive Agri-Vision: One-Click Panoptic Segmentation for Complex Crop Monitoring
brief: This project aims to develop or reproduce a Panoptic One-Click Segmentation framework specifically tailored for unstructured agricultural environments. While current Foundation Models (like SAM) excel at instance segmentation ("things" like fruits), they often struggle with semantic regions ("stuff" like ground, sky, or dense foliage) in a unified workflow. This project will implement a model that accepts sparse user prompts (single clicks) to segment both crop instances and environmental background simultaneously. The goal is to drastically reduce the data annotation time for agricultural datasets and enable "human-in-the-loop" visual reasoning for orchard robots
scope: Model Architecture: Implement a panoptic segmentation network (e.g., combining a Mask2Former or Panoptic-DeepLab backbone) integrated with an interactive Prompt Encoder (similar to SAM) to handle click inputs. Agricultural Adaptation: Fine-tune or train the model on agricultural datasets (e.g., MinneApple, CVPPP, or SugarBeets) to handle specific challenges like occlusion, variable lighting, and clustered fruits. Interaction Logic: Develop a logic layer that distinguishes whether a user's click intends to select a discrete object (fruit) or a continuous region (foliage/ground) based on feature extraction. Evaluation: Measure performance using Panoptic Quality (PQ) metrics and Number of Clicks (NoC) required to reach a target Intersection over Union (IoU) of 85%+.
requirements: Deep Learning & Computer Vision: proficiency in PyTorch; Interactive AI: Understanding of prompt engineering for vision models and loss functions for semi-supervised or weakly-supervised learning. Data Handling: Experience with COCO-format datasets and conversion tools for panoptic annotations. UI/Visualization: Ability to build a simple interactive demo (using Gradio, Streamlit, or OpenCV) to visualize the "Click -> Segment" process in real-time.

title: Explicit Truss Structure Parametrisation for Soft Robotic Grippers
brief: This project focuses on the explicit computational design of Additive Manufacturing (AM) structures for soft robotics. Rather than relying on complex implicit mathematical fields, this project restricts the design representation strictly to explicit 3D truss structures (defined networks of nodes and struts) to govern the compliance and kinematics of a soft robotic gripper. By parametrising the macro-geometry of these explicit lattices, designers can directly encode structural constraints for Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM). This straightforward approach aims to significantly reduce costly trial-and-error iterations during physical 3D printing
scope: Parametric generation and explicit 3D modelling of truss and lattice structures tailored for soft-robot morphology. Physical additive manufacturing validation using highly flexible 3D printing filaments, specifically TPU. Delivery and experimental testing of a physical soft robotic gripper within an automated grasping pipeline
requirements: CAD design, e.g. SolidWorks; Computational Design: Proficiency in parametric CAD tools (e.g., Grasshopper, Python API) to explicitly model 3D truss networks and define precise geometrical constraints. Python

title: Critical Thinking’s Resilience in the Age of Generative AI in Higher Education
brief: Over a century ago, the German philosopher Emanuel Kant defined universities as institutions dedicated to reasoning. Since then, universities have evolved, influenced by technological advancements and socio-economic challenges. Despite these changes, critical thinking remains a fundamental attribute and an essential skill for graduates. There are increasing concerns that the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) may significantly impact this aspect. Existing literature has examined this phenomenon from various perspectives and with diverse methodologies yet often fails to clearly establish or articulate the relationship through multiple disciplinary lenses, including neuroscience, psychology, and information science. This project aims to develop a conceptual framework for the key components by decomposing each factor into measurable and well-defined instruments within the context of higher education.

title: A Comparative Review of Driver Distraction Detection Using NeuroPhysiological and Eye-Tracking Signals and Vision.

title: LLM-in-the-loop Robotic Exploration
brief: This project explores the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) combined with a Generative behaviour planner (Fabric/GPSFSM) to achieve autonomous robotic exploration without relying on dedicated frontier exploration software. Students will set up an environment using the TurtleBot 4 platform, leveraging existing ROS 2 generic navigation (Nav2) and image analysis capabilities. The performance of this LLM-driven approach will be compared against traditional frontier-based exploration methods (like explore_lite), culminating in a research paper targeting robotics conferences such as ACRA.

title: Vision-Based Interactable Human Detection
brief: As robots operate in crowded social spaces, determining which humans intend to interact with the robot is challenging. This project develops a vision-based pipeline operating from the robot's point-of-view to identify and filter out bystanders versus potential interaction partners. Students will utilize object identification, skeleton tracking, and head pose/gaze estimation to assess human attention toward the robot. The system will be mounted on a physical robot platform and validated under real-world human-robot interaction scenarios. The ultimate goal is to build an efficient, deployable perception module and produce a research publication for ACRA.
scope: - Developing a vision pipeline using existing models (e.g., YOLO, OpenPose, MediaPipe) for object and skeleton detection. - Implementing gaze and face orientation estimation. - Defining a filtering algorithm to classify interactable humans based on tracking data. - Deployment and testing on standard camera hardware.

title: Audio-Based Human Interaction Detection
brief: In dynamic environments, people might approach a robot from outside its main field of vision. This project aims to create an audio-driven human interaction detection system. Utilising a microphone array or multiple independent microphones, students will implement Sound Source Localisation (SSL) and Direction of Arrival (DoA) algorithms to detect where sounds originate relative to the robot. The pipeline will also incorporate localised speech-to-text to identify if the speaker is specifically addressing the robot, allowing the robot to orient its camera stack appropriately. The outcome will be a hardware/software combined module and an ACRA paper submission.
scope: - Implementing Direction of Arrival (DoA) algorithms for a multi-microphone setup (e.g., using ODAS). - Integrating Speech-to-Text (STT) and Wake-word detection systems. - Filtering background noise and third-party conversations. - Sending orientation commands to the robot base/camera based on acoustic data.
