title: Towards a Smart Interactable Robot Platform
brief: This project focuses on the hardware and software integration required to build an interactive robotic platform. Students will design and fabricate a custom metal frame to be mounted on an LD90 base. A laptop will be mounted onto the frame to manage computation, paired with camera and audio peripherals. On the software side, students will configure this platform by integrating frameworks like Fabric, Capabilities2, and ROS 2 Nav2. The ultimate objective is a functional autonomous robot capable of basic Q&A interactions, serving as a foundation for future research and targeted for an ACRA paper.
scope: - Mechanical design and assembly of a sensor/laptop mounting frame for the LD90 base. - Integration of audio and visual peripherals. - Configuration of Fabric, FPPerception, Nav2, on ROS 2 and a Q&A software pipeline. - End-to-end system testing and performance analysis.
requirements: - ROS 2, - Linux knowledge, - Hardware Design/CAD (SolidWorks/Fusion360), - Python/C++, - Basic robotics

title: PII Scrubber for Long-term Robotic Data Logging
brief: Robots operating in public environments frequently record Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as faces and voices. For long-term human-robot interaction, robots must retain identity context while adhering to privacy requirements. This project develops a PII scrubber tool tailored for robotic datasets. The system will de-identify facial and conversational information before storage, while maintaining an encrypted or tokenised secondary database that allows authorised contextual retrieval when interacting with the same humans later. The deliverable is an open-source Python package functioning seamlessly alongside robot databases, aiming for an ACRA publication.
scope: - Developing a Python package to detect and obfuscate (blur/tokenize) faces and PII in data streams. - Implementing a database (SQLite) wrapper for linking anonymised data with collected data, such as conversational text, for storage and retrieval. - Evaluating the performance and latency of the scrubbing process during standard operations.
requirements: - Python, - Data Privacy & Security principles, - Database Management (SQL/NoSQL), - Computer Vision, Audio and STT

title: An AI Enabled Shared Family Shopping App designed for Older Adults
brief: This project aims to develop an AI-enabled shared family shopping application that supports older adults, including those experiencing mild cognitive impairment (MCI), in managing everyday grocery shopping. The app allows family members to collaboratively create, update, and monitor shopping lists in real time while providing intelligent memory-support features such as personalized reminders, frequently purchased item suggestions, voice interaction, and shopping history tracking. Designed using age-friendly and cognitively accessible principles, the application prioritizes simplicity, readability, and ease of use. The goal is to enhance independence, reduce cognitive burden, strengthen family support, and improve the overall shopping experience for older adults.
scope: The project will include the design and development of a shared, cloud-based grocery shopping application that provides real-time synchronization of shopping lists across multiple devices and users within a household. Key functionality includes: User registration, login, and household/group management. Creation of new shopping lists and modification of existing lists. Real-time synchronization of list data across smartphones, tablets, and web interfaces. Shared access for multiple household members. Add, edit, delete, and update grocery items. Search and filter grocery items within a list. Sort items by category, name, status, assigned user, or favorites. Mark items as purchased or pending. Assign categories (e.g., fruit, vegetables, dairy, cleaning products). Record item details including quantity, unit of measure, preferred brand, notes, and favorite status. Assign responsibility for purchasing specific items to nominated household members. Basic settings management (profile, notifications, accessibility preferences). Support for touch-based interaction on mobile and tablet devices. Text-based input for item entry and list management. Voice-enabled item entry and voice commands were supported by the device platform. AI-assisted features such as frequently purchased item suggestions, shopping reminders, and intelligent list recommendations. Accessibility features designed for older adults, including large text, simple navigation, high-contrast display options, and intuitive user interfaces. Secure cloud storage and backup of shopping lists and user preferences. This scope focuses on supporting collaborative household shopping, improving accessibility for older adults, and providing AI-enabled assistance to reduce memory burden and enhance independence.
requirements: Mobile and Web Application Development Database and Cloud Services (including real-time synchronisation) AI and Voice Technology Integration User Interface (UI) Design User Experience (UX) and Accessibility Design Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) for Older Adults and MCI Users Requirements Analysis and Stakeholder Engagement Agile Project Management Software Testing and Quality Assurance

title: Cognitive Workload in Multiple Tasks
brief: The Cognitive Workload in Multiple Tasks project focuses on understanding and modelling the mental effort required when individuals perform multiple tasks. The project aims to develop computational and machine learning models capable of assessing cognitive workload and predicting performance under varying task demands. By identifying patterns associated with workload fluctuations, the research seeks to enhance the design of intelligent, human-centred systems that can adapt to users' cognitive states. The outcomes of this project will contribute to improved decision-making, productivity, safety, and user experience across a range of operational and technology-driven domains.
scope: The project will include the following high-level requirements and activities: Review and analyse existing literature on cognitive workload, multitasking, and human performance. Define cognitive workload indicators and performance measures relevant to multiple-task environments. Conduct data collection activities to capture behavioural, physiological, and task performance data associated with cognitive workload. Design and implement methodologies for cognitive workload assessment and modelling. Develop computational and machine learning models to estimate, classify, and predict cognitive workload levels.
requirements: Students interested in this project should have a combination of technical, analytical, and research skills. The following skillsets are desirable: Programming and Software Development (e.g., Python, MATLAB, R, or similar programming languages). Data Analytics and Data Science including data preprocessing, feature engineering, statistical analysis, and data visualisation. Problem Solving and Critical Thinking to analyse complex research questions and develop innovative solutions. Technical Documentation and Scientific Writing for reporting findings and preparing publications or project documentation. Project Management and Teamwork Skills to support effective collaboration, planning, and delivery of project milestones.

title: Cognitive Workload Assessment in Virtual Reality Task Environments
brief: The Cognitive Workload Assessment in Virtual Reality Task Environments project investigates how cognitive workload changes when individuals perform realistic tasks within immersive virtual reality (VR) environments. The project involves the use of VR-based task simulations designed to mimic real-world activities requiring attention, decision-making, and multitasking. Cognitive workload will be assessed through behavioural, physiological, and performance measures, enabling the development of computational models that estimate workload levels during task execution. The project aims to improve understanding of human performance in immersive environments and support the design of adaptive VR systems that enhance training effectiveness, user experience, and operational performance.
scope: The project will include the following high-level requirements and activities: Review and analyse literature related to cognitive workload, virtual reality, and human performance. Collect behavioural, physiological, and task performance data during VR task execution. Investigate the impact of task complexity and environmental factors on cognitive workload. Develop methodologies for cognitive workload assessment within VR environments. Analyse the relationship between cognitive workload, user performance, and VR interaction. Document findings through reports, publications, and presentations.
requirements: Students interested in this project should possess or be willing to develop the following skills: Programming and Software Development (C#, Python, C++, or related languages). Data Analytics and Data Science including preprocessing, feature extraction, and visualisation. Statistical Analysis for performance evaluation and validation. Research and Scientific Writing for documenting and communicating results. Project Management and Team Collaboration skills.

title: Design of a Shopping List app for Lifestyle Support of People with Mild-Cognitive Impairments (MCI)
brief: We have explored how technology can facilitate independent living of people with MCI and are examining factors that influence adoption and sustained update of technology by this cohort. This project will investigate whether a set of design principles that we have devised via literature survey and participant interviews positively impact user experience via a prototyping-evaluation exercise. Through this project, you will gain experience in user-centric design processes including user evaluation.
scope: • Survey the literature and apps for seniors/people with MCI • Design and implement the shopping list mobile/PC application • User Data Analytics & Evaluation
requirements: Programming Skills; Data analytical skills; independent research skills; good reading and writing skills; every team member is expected to contribute their fair share.

title: Validation of the Virtual Reality Embodied Cognition (VREC) game as a cognitive fitness assessment tool
brief: My team has developed the VREC, intended as an assessment tool to determine severity of cognitive impairments associated with mental illnesses such as Dementia, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD). As a first step, we will need to validate VREC as a cognitive assessment tool comparable to the STROOP and 5-digit tests. The project will involve assisting the lead investigator with user studies, analysis of the compiled user data and creation of a visualization dashboard to summarize the results.
scope: • Survey the literature and related game implementations • Implement VR enhancements including the visualization dashboard • User Data Analytics & Inferences
requirements: Programming Skills; Data analytical skills; independent research skills; good reading and writing skills; every team member is expected to contribute their fair share.

title: Capstone Project Management Web Application
brief: This project aims to develop a Capstone Project Management Web Application. This application will serve as a centralized platform to streamline the administration and management of capstone projects. The application will support project allocation, proposal submissions, communication, and showcasing project outcomes. The proposed solution aims to improve efficiency and reduce administrative workload.
scope: Developing and publicly hosting a professional website.
requirements: Project management, Web development, graphic design, critical thinking, logical reasoning, teamwork, and communication.

title: Development of a Modular Cable-Driven Serial Elastic Structure with ROS2 Middleware Interface Compliance
brief: The Collaborative Robotics Lab's RAPP Lab programme explores human-robot interaction through physical theatre, treating robots as creative ensemble members rather than tools. Current work uses rigid-link industrial cobots. This project asks what a fundamentally different morphology brings to the stage. Students will design, fabricate and control a servo-actuated, tendon-driven continuum arm at the scale of a collaborative robot arm (approximately 900 mm reach). The arm must be fully modular: designed for repeated disassembly, transport and reassembly between studio and performance venues. Deliverables include the physical platform, a ROS2 control stack, and complete assembly documentation.
scope: 1. Mechanical design and CAD modelling of a multi-segment, tendon-driven continuum arm at cobot scale, with payload treated as a secondary consideration 2. A modular architecture in which every segment can be disassembled and reassembled with standard tools, verified through repeated teardown and rebuild cycles 3. Fabrication using accessible methods (3D printing, laser cutting, off the shelf servos and hardware) 4. Servo actuation electronics and embedded control, including cable tensioning and routing 5. A ROS2 (Humble) control stack exposing a standard joint-space command interface using ROS2 Moveit, with basic open-loop control based on constant-curvature kinematic assumptions 6. Scripted and teleoperated (through Xbox controller) motion demonstrations suitable for a live performance context, including basic safety behaviours (velocity limiting, soft stops, e-stop) 7. Complete technical documentation: assembly and disassembly guide, wiring diagrams, bill of materials, and software setup instructions 8. Design for forward compatibility: the command interface must be structured so that a learned motion model could drive the arm in future work using ROS2 Moveit
requirements: 1. At least one member having prior participation in a RAPP Lab workshop or project (essential). The arm is being built for a live performance research context, and familiarity with the lab's working methods, safety culture and studio environment is a prerequisite. Applicants without this background will not be considered. 2. Working ROS2 knowledge (essential): comfortable writing and debugging ROS2 and Moveit nodes in Python, using topics, services, launch files and parameters, and interfacing ROS2 with hardware over serial or a servo bus. This is not a learn-as-you-go requirement; applicants should be able to point to prior ROS2 work. 3. Hardware modelling and mechanical design (essential): proficiency in parametric CAD (Fusion 360, SolidWorks or similar), design for 3D printing and laser cutting, and tolerance-aware design for parts that must survive repeated assembly and disassembly. 4. Embedded and electronics competence: microcontroller programming, servo control (PWM or a bus protocol such as Dynamixel), wiring and power budgeting. 5. Mathematical maturity: willingness to engage with continuum kinematics (constant-curvature models) at the level of implementing them in code. 6. Version control and documentation discipline: all design files and code under Git, with documentation treated as a first-class deliverable rather than an afterthought. Team roles will span mechanical, electronics and software streams, but every team member is expected to meet the ROS2 and RAPP Lab criteria.

title: Augmented Reality version of the Virtual Reality Embodied Cognition (VREC) tool
brief: We have developed a Virtual Reality version of the BATAK lightboard game, with potential mental health applications. The purpose of this project would be to develop an Augmented Reality alternative of the game (developed with a Hololens), so that the game can be combined with rehabilitation robotics for stroke rehabilitation. You will need to *submit your code* as part of your project deliverables, and this condition is non-negotiable.
scope: • Survey the literature and related game implementations • Design and Implement the AR application • User Data Analytics & Evaluation
requirements: Programming Skills; Data analytical skills; independent research skills; good reading and writing skills; every team member is expected to contribute their fair share.

title: Advanced Machine Learning Models for Robust sEMG Gesture Recognition and Robotic Hand Control
brief: This project focuses on the core machine learning and data science challenges of using surface electromyography (sEMG) for human-robot interaction. Biomedical signals like sEMG are notoriously noisy and suffer from significant cross-subject variance and muscle fatigue degradation. Rather than focusing on hardware, students will focus on developing and optimising advanced machine learning and deep learning models (e.g., CNNs, LSTMs, or Attention mechanisms) to achieve highly accurate and generalisable gesture classification. The project emphasises high-dimensional feature engineering, domain adaptation (transfer learning across different users - stretch goal), and optimising models for real-time inference latency. The final optimised algorithms will be deployed to drive a physical robotic hand, demonstrating the practical robustness of the developed models.
scope: Advanced Feature Representation: Implementing time-frequency feature extraction (e.g., Wavelet Transforms, Spectrograms) and applying dimensionality reduction techniques (e.g., PCA, t-SNE) to process high-dimensional multi-channel data. Deep Learning Model Development: Designing, training, and tuning advanced neural network architectures tailored for time-series physiological data, comparing them against classical baselines (SVM, Random Forest). Cross-Subject Generalisation: Investigating transfer learning, few-shot learning, or domain adaptation techniques to improve model accuracy on new, unseen users without requiring extensive recalibration datasets. Real-Time Inference Optimisation: Profiling and optimising the trained models (e.g., through quantisation or efficient sliding-window architectures) to ensure low-latency, real-time prediction stability. System Deployment: Integrating the optimised machine learning pipeline with a basic communication interface to actuate a physical robotic hand based on live gesture predictions.
requirements: Advanced Machine Learning & Deep Learning: Strong proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch or TensorFlow), with an understanding of sequence modelling and neural network optimisation. Data Science & Analytics: Expertise in handling noisy time-series datasets, statistical performance evaluation (e.g., k-fold cross-validation, precision-recall analysis), and managing class imbalances. MLOps & Deployment: Understanding of real-time algorithmic pipelines, decision smoothing logic (e.g., majority voting, confidence thresholding), and translating offline models to online inference. Basic System Integration: Ability to interface Python-based predictive models with external hardware via standard communication protocols (e.g., Serial, UDP, or basic ROS2 wrappers).

title: Decoding Visual Perception from Brain Signals using Deep Learning
brief: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) enable communication between the human brain and computers by interpreting neural activity. Recent advances have demonstrated the possibility of reconstructing visual experiences directly from electroencephalography (EEG) signals. This project aims to develop a prototype system that decodes dynamic visual information from EEG recordings using deep learning techniques. Students will utilise a publicly available dataset and investigate temporal neural representations for predicting video content or semantic attributes from EEG signals. The project combines machine learning, computer vision, signal processing and generative AI, providing practical experience in developing intelligent neuro-inspired systems for next-generation human-computer interaction applications.
scope: Expected Deliverables: -Literature review on EEG-based visual perception decoding and brain–computer interfaces. -A project report written in research paper style that includes: (1) Whole processing pipeline and system architecture. (2) Deep learning model for decoding visual information from EEG signals (e.g., object category, scene type, or semantic attributes). (3) Performance evaluation against baseline machine learning or deep learning models using standard evaluation metrics. (4) Visualisation and analysis of decoded visual representations and model performance. (5) This final project report should describe the methodology, experimental results, limitations, and future work. -Well-documented source code. -A prototype demonstrating EEG-based visual perception decoding. The project will include the following high-level requirements and activities: -Review literature on EEG-based visual decoding and brain-computer interfaces. -Install and configure the development environment. -Obtain and preprocess a publicly available EEG dataset. -Perform EEG preprocessing, including filtering, normalization, and segmentation. -Extract temporal/spectral EEG representations using deep learning models. -Implement one or more baseline neural decoding models. -Predict semantic information (e.g., object category, motion, colour) from EEG signals. -Evaluate model performance using suitable metrics. -Visualise learned EEG representations and prediction results. -Compare experimental results with published baseline models. -Produce technical documentation and a demonstration of the developed prototype.
requirements: This project involves massive programming and deep learning. It is suitable for students who have a solid background in Machine Learning. Essential: -Python programming -Machine Learning fundamentals -Deep Learning (PyTorch preferred) -GPU programming (CUDA) -Basic signal processing -Data analysis and visualisation -Git version control Desirable -Computer Vision -Time-series analysis -EEG signal processing -Transformers or sequence models -Experience with PyTorch Lightning or HuggingFace -Basic knowledge of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI)

title: EmoSens: Multimodal Emotion Recognition using EEG and Physiological Signals
brief: Emotion recognition plays an increasingly important role in intelligent human-computer interaction, healthcare, education, and collaborative robotics. While facial expressions and speech are commonly used for emotion recognition, physiological signals such as electroencephalography (EEG), electrocardiography (ECG), and electrodermal activity (EDA) provide objective measures of a person's internal emotional state. This project aims to develop a multimodal deep learning system that integrates EEG with complementary physiological or behavioural signals to improve emotion recognition accuracy and robustness. Students will investigate multimodal data fusion techniques and evaluate machine learning models using publicly available datasets, contributing to the development of more adaptive and human-centred intelligent systems.
scope: Expected Deliverables: -Literature review on multimodal emotion recognition -A report in research paper style that includes: (1) Physiological signal preprocessing pipeline (2) Baseline unimodal emotion recognition models (3) Multimodal fusion framework (4) Experimental comparison of fusion strategies (5) Performance evaluation using standard metrics -Source code with documentation -A demonstration The project will include the following high-level requirements and activities: -Conduct a literature review on affective computing and multimodal emotion recognition. -Select and study one or more public emotion recognition datasets (e.g., DEAP, MAHNOB-HCI, SEED-IV, SEED-V). -Preprocess EEG signals and additional modalities such as ECG, EDA, facial expressions, eye gaze, or respiration. -Extract features using signal processing and deep learning techniques. -Develop unimodal baseline emotion recognition models. -Design and implement multimodal fusion strategies (early fusion, late fusion, or attention-based fusion). -Train and evaluate deep learning models for emotion classification. -Compare different modality combinations and fusion methods. -Visualise learned feature representations and model predictions. -Document the developed system and experimental findings.
requirements: Essential: -Python programming -Machine Learning fundamentals -Deep Learning (PyTorch or TensorFlow) -Data preprocessing and visualisation -Basic signal processing -Git version control Desirable: -EEG signal analysis -Physiological signal processing (ECG, EDA, PPG) -Computer Vision (for facial expression recognition) -Multimodal deep learning -Attention mechanisms and Transformers -Time-series analysis -GPU computing -Experience with MNE-Python or NeuroKit2

title: Development of a Multimodal Physiological Signal Acquisition and Visualisation Platform
brief: Multimodal physiological sensing is increasingly used in human–computer interaction, affective computing, and brain–computer interface research. However, collecting synchronised data from multiple sensing devices often requires substantial software development and integration. This project aims to develop a unified multimodal data acquisition platform capable of simultaneously collecting electroencephalography (EEG), electrocardiography (ECG), electrodermal activity (GSR), and webcam-based eye-tracking data. The platform will provide real-time signal acquisition, stream synchronisation, preprocessing, visualisation, data storage, and an intuitive graphical user interface. The completed system will serve as a reusable research platform for future multimodal sensing and artificial intelligence studies.
scope: Expected Deliverables: -Modular multimodal signal acquisition software supporting EEG, ECG, GSR, and webcam-based eye tracking. -Real-time signal synchronisation framework for multiple sensor streams. -Signal preprocessing modules for filtering, normalisation, and basic artefact removal. -Interactive graphical user interface for experiment control and device management. -Real-time dashboard for visualising physiological signals. -Data recording system with synchronised timestamps and experiment metadata. -Software architecture documentation and user manual. -Demonstration of simultaneous multimodal data acquisition and recording. -Final project report documenting the system design, implementation, testing, and future extensions. The project will include the following high-level requirements and activities: -Conduct a review of multimodal physiological sensing platforms and communication protocols. -Develop software interfaces for acquiring signals from EEG, ECG, GSR, and webcam-based eye-tracking devices. -Implement a unified data acquisition framework capable of collecting multiple signal streams simultaneously. -Develop a signal synchronisation mechanism using timestamps or a common system clock. -Implement basic real-time preprocessing, including filtering, resampling, and artefact handling where appropriate. -Design a modular architecture to support future integration of additional sensing devices. -Develop a graphical user interface (GUI) for experiment configuration, device management, signal monitoring, and recording control. -Implement real-time visualisation of multiple physiological signals. -Design an efficient data storage format with synchronised timestamps and experiment metadata. -Validate the platform through multimodal data collection experiments. -Produce comprehensive software documentation and a user manual.
requirements: Essential: -Programming (Python) -Object-oriented software development -GUI development -Software architecture and modular design -Data structures and file management -Git version control Desirable: -Signal processing fundamentals -Serial communication and Bluetooth APIs -Webcam programming (OpenCV) -EEG and physiological signal processing -Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) -Multithreading or asynchronous programming -Data visualisation libraries (PyQtGraph, Matplotlib)

title: Learning Emotion Transition Patterns from EEG Signals using Graph Neural Networks
brief: Emotions are dynamic processes that evolve continuously over time rather than occurring as isolated states. Conventional EEG-based emotion recognition methods typically classify each time segment independently, overlooking temporal dependencies between emotional states. This project aims to develop a graph neural network (GNN) framework to learn emotion transition patterns directly from EEG signals. The project will evaluate whether graph-based temporal modelling improves emotion recognition accuracy, robustness, and interpretability compared with conventional deep learning approaches.
scope: Expected Deliverables: -Literature review -EEG preprocessing pipeline -Temporal graph construction module -Graph neural network implementation -Experimental comparison with baseline methods -Visualisation of learned emotion transition patterns -Source code with documentation -Final report and project demonstration The project will include the following high-level requirements and activities: -Conduct a literature review on EEG-based emotion recognition and graph neural networks. -Select and preprocess a publicly available EEG emotion dataset (e.g., DEAP, SEED-IV, or SEED-V). -Perform EEG preprocessing, including filtering, segmentation, and normalisation. -Extract EEG features using conventional signal processing or deep learning techniques. -Construct temporal graphs from sequential EEG segments. -Implement a Graph Neural Network (e.g., GCN or Graph Attention Network) to model temporal dependencies. -Compare the proposed model against baseline methods such as CNNs, LSTMs, or Transformers. -Evaluate performance using standard emotion recognition metrics. -Visualise learned emotion transition patterns and graph attention weights. -Develop a demonstration system and technical documentation.
requirements: Essential: -Python programming -Machine Learning fundamentals -Deep Learning (PyTorch preferred) -Data analysis and visualisation -Basic signal processing -Git version control Desirable: -EEG signal processing -Graph Neural Networks (PyTorch Geometric or DGL) -Time-series analysis -Computer Vision or Human–Computer Interaction -GPU programming (CUDA)

title: Accountable Design-to-Engineering Translation for a University Consultation-Booking System
brief: This capstone project will design a proposed web-based consultation-booking system for university students. It adopts a Design Science approach to apply an accountable translation framework when developing and evaluating system-design artefacts. The framework connects user and stakeholder evidence with requirements, interface designs, data models, and technical decisions. It uses artefact mapping, provenance tracking, and gap-flagging to maintain inspectable relationships across design activities. Students will develop and evaluate a high-fidelity interactive Figma prototype. They will also produce supporting requirements, architecture, data, privacy, security, accessibility, testing, and decision artefacts. The project sponsor will provide guidance on applying the framework.
scope: • Define the design problem, objectives, and context. • Review relevant literature and established design knowledge. • Collect and analyse requirements from capstone students and academics, subject to applicable university requirements. • Develop user profiles, journey maps, requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria. • Apply the accountable translation framework, including artefact mapping, provenance tracking, and gap-flagging. • Design booking, rescheduling, cancellation, and confirmation workflows. • Develop a high-fidelity interactive Figma prototype. • Develop a conceptual data model, system architecture, and processing specifications. • Specify privacy, security, validation, and accessibility requirements. • Evaluate the prototype and related system-design artefacts using feedback from capstone students and academics, requirements-based checks, accessibility and usability inspections, and realistic scenarios. All stakeholder engagement must meet applicable university requirements. • Document design decisions, sources, transformations, responsibilities, unresolved gaps, limitations, and design-to-engineering relationships. • Integrate the artefacts into a final report, presentation, and poster.
requirements: Skills in business and systems analysis, requirements analysis, UX design, system modelling, project management, teamwork, and technical communication. Some familiarity with Figma is desirable, but students can develop the required prototyping skills during the project. No advanced programming skills are required.

title: Human-Centred Design of a University Consultation-Booking System Using Established Practices
brief: This capstone project will design a proposed web-based consultation-booking system for university students. It adopts a Design Science approach to develop and evaluate system-design artefacts using established development practices. The team will select and justify suitable approaches drawn from human-centred design, UX design, Agile, Scrum, requirements analysis, prototyping, backlog management, and system design. Students will develop and evaluate a high-fidelity interactive Figma prototype. They will also produce supporting requirements, architecture, data, privacy, security, accessibility, testing, project-management, and decision artefacts. The project emphasises coherent integration across these artefacts using the selected practices.
scope: • Define the design problem, objectives, and context. • Review relevant literature and established design knowledge. • Select and justify suitable human-centred, UX, Agile, requirements, and system-design practices. • Collect and analyse requirements from capstone students and academics, subject to applicable university requirements. • Develop user profiles, journey maps, requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria. • Create and maintain appropriate backlog, project, issue, version, and decision records. • Design booking, rescheduling, cancellation, and confirmation workflows. • Develop a high-fidelity interactive Figma prototype. • Develop a conceptual data model, system architecture, and processing specifications. • Specify privacy, security, validation, and accessibility requirements. • Evaluate the prototype and related system-design artefacts using feedback from capstone students and academics, requirements-based checks, accessibility and usability inspections, and realistic scenarios. All stakeholder engagement must meet applicable university requirements. • Document design decisions, limitations, and relationships among the developed artefacts. • Integrate the artefacts into a final report, presentation, and poster.
requirements: Skills in business and systems analysis, requirements analysis, UX design, system modelling, project management, teamwork, and technical communication. Some familiarity with Figma is desirable, but students can develop the required prototyping skills during the project. No advanced programming skills are required.

title: Student-AI Hybrid Teams: A Framework for Validating GenAI’s Contributions in Group Work
brief: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has brought about an unprecedented disruption to the higher education sector, facilitating opportunities for personalised learning, supporting research and writing, and providing instant clarification and feedback to mention a few. However, the ubiquity and accessibly to GenAI services has presented several challenges, particularly for academic integrity and increasing reliance on GenAI in assessments. Higher education institutes have since responded with several strategies to facilitate development of AI literacy while miniating the integrity of our courses and graduate learning. In response to GenAI use in assessments, the University of Canberra has introduced in 2026 a 3-tier system: permitted, guided, or restricted. Within the ‘guided’ strategy, students are now encouraged, and in some cases required, to utilise GenAI tools and services as a resource in the completion of assessment tasks, but within a guided framework outlining where and how GenAI can be used.
scope: - Conduct a literature review on the adoption of GenAI in higher education, with focus on current practices for validating GenAI content and contributions, particularly in teamwork. - Run a short internal survey for how ITS students validate GenAI content in group assessments. - Develop a practical GenAI validation framework for GenAI output validation and associated artefacts that can be adopted in group assessments while also maintaining individual team member accountability. - Time permitting, pilot test the framework in at least one assessment in unit Corporate Strategy and IT Governance in S2 2026.
requirements: - Research skills (ideally completed unit ICT and Engineering Research Methodology 12090 PG) - Literature review and writeup - Survey design skills - Quantitative analysis skills (statistical analysis) - Qualitative analysis skills (thematic analysis) - Team management

title: Beyond Digital Literacy: Evolving Expectations for Digital Native ICT Gradates in the AI Era
brief: The mass adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping the workplace and setting an increasing expectation for university graduates to be able to work with GenAI tools and applications effectively and ethically. Accordingly, there is now rising expectation from employers that university graduates who are digital natives now possess AI literacy skills as well, a skill set that builds on digital literacy (ability to create and/or use digital technologies) but also extend into a capability to develop and work with AI and GenAI tools and services, ethically and responsibly. This places pressure on universities to prepare graduates who can demonstrate AI literacy skills, at least at foundational and/or intermediate levels. The question then is what is AI literacy? How is this skillset different from digital literacy? Therefore, this research project aims to investigate these two skill areas and develop a proposal for practical strategies that can be implemented by educators to bridge the gap between the two within the student’s time at a university.
scope: - Conduct a literature review on digital literacy and AI literacy. - Develop a matrix that shows the capabilities within each literacy area. - Identify the gaps (common areas and new areas related to use of AI technologies). - Compile a set of use cases and practices for university educators (unit conveners and teachers) who can help students develop this skillset and bridge the gap between the two.
requirements: Research skills (ideally completed unit ICT and Engineering Research Methodology 12090 PG). Literature review writing and knowledge of systematic literature review frameworks. Gap analysis capability. Visualization skills. Team management.

title: Implementing an assessment submission reminder module for Canvas
brief: Currently, course conveners need to manually send out/schedule assessment submission reminders to students. The project involves adding an automated reminder module to the Canvas web and/or Canvas mobile versions by looking up reminders on the Canvas assessments page.
scope: • Survey the literature and related game implementations • Design and Implement the Canvas application • App Evaluation
requirements: Programming Skills; Data analytical skills; independent research skills; good reading and writing skills; every team member is expected to contribute their fair share.

title: Designing a Quantum-Ready Government Procurement Decision Support System
brief: Government agencies increasingly rely on digital procurement systems to support complex purchasing decisions involving supplier evaluation, risk assessment, compliance, and value for money. Emerging technologies such as Quantum Artificial Intelligence (QAI) may enhance future analytical capabilities, but existing procurement systems are not designed to accommodate hybrid quantum–classical approaches. This capstone project adopts a Design Science approach to design and evaluate a proposed quantum-ready government procurement decision support system. Students will develop a high-fidelity interactive Figma prototype together with supporting system-design artefacts using sponsor-provided documentation and relevant secondary literature. The project emphasises transparent, explainable, and quantum-ready procurement decision support.
scope: • Define the design problem, objectives, and organisational context. • Review relevant literature and established design knowledge. • Analyse the Sponsor Project Initiation Document and derive functional and non-functional requirements. • Design the proposed procurement decision support system, including its architecture, workflows, data, and user interactions. • Develop and evaluate a high-fidelity interactive Figma prototype together with supporting system-design artefacts. • Incorporate governance, privacy, security, accessibility, explainability, and quantum-readiness considerations into the proposed design. • Evaluate the proposed system design using realistic procurement scenarios and appropriate analytical evaluation methods. • Integrate the developed artefacts into a final report, presentation, and poster.
requirements: Skills in business and systems analysis, requirements analysis, UX design, system modelling, project management, teamwork, and technical communication. Some familiarity with Figma is desirable, but students can develop the required prototyping skills during the project. No advanced programming or quantum computing skills are required.

title: Multimodal Biometric Fusion: machine Learning for Iris and Fingerprint Authentication
brief: This project develops a multimodal biometric authentication system using a combined kaggle dataset of iris and fingerprint scans. The dataset contains high-resolution biometric information from 45 individuals, comprising 10 iris scans (5 left eye, 5 right eye) and 10 fingerprint scans (one per finger) per person. Because the data volume is constrained, students will focus on few-shot learning and transfer learning techniques to prevent model overfitting. The core objective is to extract and fuse the intricate details of iris patterns and fingerprint ridges to create a highly robust identity verification system suitable for high-security access control or healthcare patient identification.
scope: Data Pipeline Engineering: Building multi-input data loaders that correctly pair an individual's left/right iris scans with their corresponding fingerprint scans for unified training. Feature Extraction: Utilising computer vision techniques and pre-trained deep learning models (e.g., ResNet, MobileNet) to extract distinct features from high-resolution iris images and fingerprint ridge patterns. Multimodal Fusion Design: Implementing and comparing different fusion architectures (such as feature-level concatenation or decision-level score fusion) to combine the separate biometric modalities into a single identity prediction. Few-Shot Learning & Regularisation: Applying aggressive data augmentation, transfer learning, or Siamese network architectures to achieve high accuracy despite having only 20 total images per person.
requirements: Computer Vision & Deep Learning: Strong proficiency in PyTorch or TensorFlow, with an understanding of how to implement pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image classification. Data Science & Statistics: Ability to manage complex data distributions, handle class-matching logic for multiple inputs, and plot advanced evaluation curves (e.g., ROC curves, Equal Error Rate). Algorithm Optimisation: Understanding of techniques to combat overfitting on small datasets, including dropout, batch normalisation, and advanced image augmentation strategies.

title: Understanding communication through digital presentations
brief: Effectively communicating via digital (or powerpoint) presentations is certainly an art; how to get your message across to a student cohort in a lecture, or within a few minutes to the executive board that is short on time may take a significant amount of iterations and rehearsals; we would like to explore if there is a 'science' leveraged by expert presenters via data-centered plus user-centered approaches. The project will be offered with Dr. Naru Srinivasaraghavan, Director, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
scope: • Survey the literature. • Compile a set of good and bad audio-visual presentations. • Employ machine learning to identify discriminative patterns between the two classes.
requirements: Programming Skills; Data analytical skills; independent research skills; good reading and writing skills; every team member is expected to contribute their fair share.

title: AI-Enabled Multilingual Video Processing and Social Media Publishing Automation
brief: This project aims to design and develop an automated multilingual video processing and publishing system using n8n and related technologies. Videos stored in Google Drive will be processed to generate transcripts and subtitles, translate captions into selected languages, prepare appropriate video outputs, and publish content to selected social media platforms such as YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn. Google Sheets will provide a user-friendly interface for configuring, controlling and monitoring the workflow, including platform and language selection and publishing status. The project will investigate free cloud-based and open-source technologies, with locally hosted processing used where suitable free cloud solutions are unavailable.
scope: The project includes requirements analysis, system architecture, development, integration, testing and documentation of an automated video processing and publishing pipeline. High-level activities include: • Designing modular n8n workflows integrating Google Drive and Google Sheets. • Developing a Google Sheets-based control and monitoring interface for managing videos, languages, publishing destinations and workflow status. • Automatically detecting or retrieving videos stored in designated Google Drive locations. • Extracting audio and generating timestamped speech-to-text transcripts. • Generating subtitle/caption files and translating captions into multiple user-selected languages. • Investigating both embedded (“burned-in”) captions and platform-supported subtitle tracks. • Processing and formatting video outputs as required for different publishing platforms. • Integrating publishing workflows for platforms such as YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn, subject to available APIs and platform access. • Recording processing status, generated files, errors and published URLs back into Google Sheets. • Investigating human-in-the-loop review and approval prior to publication. • Investigating free cloud, open-source and locally hosted technologies for transcription, translation and video processing. • Implementing appropriate authentication, credential management, error handling, logging and retry mechanisms. • Developing a modular architecture that can be extended to additional languages, platforms and content-processing capabilities in the future. • Producing technical documentation and a handover package enabling future teams to continue development.
requirements: Students would benefit from a combination of the following skills and interests: • Workflow automation and n8n • Systems analysis and requirements engineering • Software and API integration • REST APIs, webhooks and authentication/OAuth • Google Drive and Google Sheets integration • JavaScript and/or Python • Video and audio processing, including FFmpeg • Speech-to-text and transcription technologies • Artificial intelligence and machine learning • Natural language processing and machine translation • Cloud computing and/or local/self-hosted services • Database/data management concepts • Information security and credential management • Testing, debugging, logging and error handling • Agile software development and project management • User experience and human-in-the-loop workflow design • Technical documentation and system architecture Students are not expected to possess all these skills at commencement. The project is particularly suitable for a multidisciplinary team interested in AI, automation, systems integration and practical software engineering.
